parsed.explanation: The operative regime shows no entry bar, but after arrival the state is itself the threat: documented police profiling and group detention of trans women (Aug 2025), ~299 detention decisions in 2025, a prison system placing trans prisoners by birth sex with strip searches, isolation, restricted healthcare and a custody death followed by investigative delay and impunity; a knifing whose victim was referred for arrest; no gender-identity protection; pending criminalisation drafts; and senior-official demonisation. This is state-tolerated targeting with lethal custody outcomes and no working remedy — worse than 0.35 anchors, at the lighter edge of the 0.25 band given short detentions and no execution evidence for visitors.

entry_documents.exposure: No LGBTQ-specific entry bar; general rule requiring original photo ID at transit checkpoints with fines and detention warnings creates outing friction for a trans visitor whose documents and presentation diverge.
entry_documents.interaction: The ID rule hands police a lawful stop lever; the August 2025 detentions show exactly this lever used against trans women.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented profiling detentions of ~20 trans women ('documented us' before any law passed); 299 detention decisions in 2025; prison placement by registered sex, strip searches, isolation, restricted care, and a trans prisoner's death with delayed response and no witness statements taken.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None; complaints can lead to further violence.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor ID stop can escalate into the documented custodial track; short-term holding conditions for trans detainees not sourced.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Binary, heteronormative prison administration with no policy or staff training for LGBTI+ needs; trans man held in women's prison; hospital access avoided for fear of other prisoners.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Any detention (even administrative) places a trans visitor in the birth-sex custody track.

care_services.exposure: HRT not covered by public healthcare; visitors must pay privately. Health-ministry regulation routes transition documentation through a named 'gender reassignment' category, creating profiling risk.
care_services.protection: Surgery available in several major cities.
care_services.interaction: Medication continuity depends on private arrangements; a care-seeking visitor enters the profiling-relevant medical-board data trail.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Head of government frames LGBTQ people as a threat to children ('Decade of Family and Population'); draft package would criminalise LGBT people; raids on 9 associations and 13 businesses; broadcasting regulator censors LGBTQ content; association dissolved and founders on trial.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: A proposed 'biological sex' advocacy offence was dropped from the 2026 package; symbolic same-sex weddings possible but without status.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official demonisation legitimises police profiling and emboldens private hostility a visitor encounters.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for trans minors or travelling guardians specifically; child-protection rhetoric drives raids and could colour scrutiny of a trans adult travelling with a minor.
minors_guardians.interaction: State 'protecting children' framing is the stated rationale for enforcement sweeps.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Six deaths linked to anti-LGBTQ violence in 2025 (three hate killings); a trans woman knifed while her attacker was released and she was referred for arrest — documented policing asymmetry; historical pattern of beatings and robberies against trans people.
street_violence_police_response.protection: None; rights groups and an MP demanded independent investigation only.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Reporting violence as a trans visitor risks the documented victim-arrest asymmetry.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No SOGI non-discrimination law; no hate-crime recourse; 2023 case on ineffective remedies pending since 2023; regional bloc found protections insufficient; demonstrations for exclusion officially permitted.
remedies_unknowns.protection: None operative; Article 5 challenge outcome unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: No working remedy at any stage; unknowns (draft law's fate, holding-cell conditions) resolve toward the structural risk, not neutrality.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-C features organised morality sweeps with custodial violence and coercive charging. Here profiling detentions and lethal custody outcomes are documented but visitors are typically released without charge, no execution pathway is shown, and charging is not yet enacted — this sits at that anchor's lighter edge, above 0.25.

Very close: raids, detention, fines, ineffective courts, no execution. This dossier adds a custody death with impunity signals and quantified state-tolerated violence (six deaths), pushing to the top of the 0.25 band rather than above it.

0.35-B tops out at hours-long detention with no lethal force. This regime exceeds it: lethal violence with policing asymmetry, documented deadly custody conditions, and no effective remedy anywhere — so materially below 0.35-B.
0.55-B's worst outcome is refused entry and humiliation with functioning appeal desks. Here remedies are absent, detention is routine and custody is dangerous; far below.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller-facing regime is defined not by entry law but by what follows discovery: documented police profiling of trans women using ID-check powers, mass detention decisions, and a custodial system that places trans people by birth sex with isolation, strip searches, restricted care, and a death met with investigative delay. State rhetoric actively frames LGBTQ people as threats, a criminalisation draft is pending, and there is no discrimination or hate-crime recourse anywhere in the chain — reporting violence risks the documented victim-arrest asymmetry. Combined, this is state-tolerated targeting (tier 2) with documented tier-4/5 custody outcomes and no operative protection, placing the jurisdiction at the top of the High Risk band; the unresolved draft law and unknown holding-cell conditions extrapolate downward, not toward neutrality.
